name: Weak or broken cryptographic primitive (DES/RC4/ECB/MD5/SHA1)
task_triggers: encrypting or hashing data in iOS/macOS
implementing signing, integrity, or password hashing
attack_scenario: An attacker recovers or forges data: ECB reveals repeated plaintext blocks in ciphertext, DES/RC4 keys are brute-forceable, and MD5/SHA-1 collisions let an attacker craft two inputs with the same digest to defeat integrity checks or signature verification.
negative_test_hint: encrypt the repeating-block plaintext "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA" and assert the code uses AES with a random IV rather than DES/RC4/ECB, so identical plaintext blocks never yield identical ciphertext

exemplar.explanation: DES/3DES/RC4 are broken ciphers and ECB mode leaks plaintext structure because identical blocks encrypt identically; MD5 and SHA-1 are collision-broken and unsuitable for integrity or signatures. AES with a random IV and SHA-256 provide real confidentiality and collision resistance, as required by OWASP MASVS-CRYPTO and CWE-327/CWE-328.
